title: Part-of-Speech Swapping Trap
description: Examiner question mein Adjective poochta hai aur Option A mein usi word-family ka Noun rakh deta hai.
incorrectExample: Question: Find the synonym of PRUDENT (Adj). Candidate marks: 'Prudence' (Noun).
trapRule: A noun can NEVER be the synonym or antonym of an adjective. Suffix -ence/-ance indicates a noun; suffix -ent/-ant indicates an adjective.

title: Secondary Literal Sense Trap in Polysemic Words
description: Sentence context mein word figurative/legal hota hai, lekin candidate dictionary ka primary physical meaning tick kar deta hai.
incorrectExample: Sentence: 'The magistrate delivered a SOUND judgment.' Candidate marks: 'Audible / Noisy'.
trapRule: Always freeze the active contextual sense of polysemic words (sound, grave, plain, sharp, fine) from the sentence before inspecting options.

title: The 'Invaluable' Pseudo-Negative Trap
description: Candidate prefix 'in-' dekhkar samajhta hai ki word negative hai, aur 'invaluable' ka meaning 'worthless' samajh leta hai.
incorrectExample: Candidate assumption: Invaluable = Not valuable = Cheap / Worthless.
correctExample: Fact: Invaluable = Beyond valuation, extremely precious, priceless. Antonym: 'Worthless' or 'Valueless'.
trapRule: 'Invaluable' means so precious that its monetary value cannot be computed. Its antonym is strictly 'Worthless'.

title: The 'Inflammable' False Contrast Trap
description: Candidate assume karta hai ki 'Flammable' aag pakadta hai aur 'Inflammable' fireproof hota hai.
incorrectExample: Candidate assumption: Inflammable is the opposite of Flammable.
correctExample: Fact: 'Inflammable' and 'Flammable' are exact SYNONYMS (both mean easily ignited). The true antonym is 'Non-flammable'.
trapRule: Prefix 'in-' here is an intensive derived from Latin 'inflammare' (to inflame), NOT a negative marker.

title: The 'Disinterested' vs 'Uninterested' Neutrality Trap
description: Candidate 'disinterested' ko 'uninterested' (bored, not caring) samajhne ki bhool karta hai.
incorrectExample: Sentence: 'A judge must be disinterested.' Candidate interprets: 'The judge is bored and indifferent.'
correctExample: Fact: 'Disinterested' means impartial, unbiased, having no financial stake in the outcome. Antonym: 'Biased' or 'Prejudiced'.
trapRule: Uninterested = lacking interest / bored. Disinterested = impartial / unbiased. In court contexts, 'disinterested' is always a virtue.

title: Intermediate Degree vs Polar Scale Opposite Trap
description: Gradable spectrum par candidate scale extreme ka opposite kisi weaker/intermediate point ko maan leta hai.
incorrectExample: Question: Antonym of HOT. Candidate marks: 'Warm' or 'Tepid'.
trapRule: Intermediate shades on a continuum are not antonyms. The antonym of 'Furious' is 'Calm', not 'Annoyed'.

title: Tone & Valence Neglect (Praise vs Criticism)
description: Candidate denotation dekh leta hai lekin ye bhool jata hai ki ek word positive hai aur doosra derogatory insult hai.
incorrectExample: Treating 'Economical' (sensible, positive) as synonymous with 'Miserly / Stingy' (selfish, negative).
trapRule: Synonym selection requires matching the emotional valence (+ / - / neutral) of the target word.

title: Out-of-Register Substitution Trap
description: Informal conversational words ko formal legal ya administrative sentences mein swap karna.
incorrectExample: Sentence: 'The High Court decided to ______ proceedings.' Option chosen: 'Start' (Colloquial).
trapRule: High Court exam questions strictly assess institutional formal register. Colloquial synonyms are deliberate distractors.

title: Prompt Polarity Inversion (Synonym vs Antonym Rushing)
description: Question mein 'ANTONYM' manga hota hai, lekin candidate Option A mein diya gaya mashhoor synonym mark kar deta hai.
incorrectExample: Question: Choose the ANTONYM of CANDOR. Option A: 'Frankness'. Candidate marks Option A.
trapRule: Always physically underline the words 'SYNONYM' or 'ANTONYM' in the question stem before looking at options.

title: Phonetic Prefix Guesswork Error
description: Phonetic assimilation rules na janne ki wajah se invalid fabricated words select karna.
correctExample: Correct Forms: 'Illegal' (il- before l), 'Irregular' (ir- before r), 'Irresponsible' (ir- before r).
trapRule: im- precedes bilabials (p, m); il- precedes l; ir- precedes r; in- precedes vowels and alveolar consonants.

title: Context Blindness in Figurative Language
description: Metaphorical ya abstract usage ko ignore karke literal physical option select karna.
incorrectExample: Sentence: 'She has a LUCID mind.' Candidate marks: 'Transparent / Glass-like'.
trapRule: When adjectives qualify abstract nouns (mind, argument, doctrine), their figurative intellectual sense governs.

title: Antonym Overextension in Complementary Pairs
description: Strict binary complementary opposites ko gradable scale ki tarah treat karna.
incorrectExample: Thinking something can be 'partially mortal' or 'fairly dead'.
correctExample: Complementary pairs (Alive/Dead, Valid/Void, Pass/Fail) admit zero middle ground.
trapRule: Complementary opposites cannot take degree adverbs like 'very', 'fairly', or 'somewhat'.
